t: You're looking at St Dunstan-in-the-West on Fleet Street. The church has medieval origins, but the building you see, with its octagonal nave, was put up in the 1830s to designs by John Shaw, who often worked in Gothic Revival style. Several people are buried here. Thomas Campion was a composer, poet and physician who wrote over a hundred lute songs. George Calvert, the first Baron Baltimore, was a Secretary of State who publicly declared his Catholicism. Richard Hoare founded C. Hoare and Co., the oldest bank in Britain still operating. The physician Edward Dodding and the judge William Portman rest here too.
